## The comparison table Set the size filter to 1M+ episodes and one row remains; sort by Hours to compare published durations. Episodes and hours measure different things, because a trajectory can last eight seconds or eight minutes. RoboMIND reports 305.5 hours for its 107k-trajectory cohort, which mixes real and simulated data . NVIDIA's open Physical AI dataset reports both, 15 terabytes and more than 320,000 trajectories . ## Open X-Embodiment: breadth by federation OXE pooled 60 existing datasets from 34 labs into one standardized RLDS format: over a million trajectories spanning 22 robot embodiments, 527 skills and 160,266 tasks . RLDS is a standard, lossless episode format for sharing and reusing datasets . RT-1-X trained on the pool beat each small-scale domain's original method by 50% on average, but underperformed RT-1 trained on a large-scale domain's own data, which the authors attribute to underfitting. The higher-capacity RT-2-X roughly tripled performance on out-of-distribution skills over the same model trained without the pool . Generalist policies train on it ([VLA models](/manipulation/vla-models)): Octo used 800k OXE trajectories , and OpenVLA used 970k real-world demonstrations . Later cross-embodiment pools are larger or broader. ARIO reports about 3 million episodes across 321,064 tasks , and CrossFormer trained one policy on 900K trajectories from 20 embodiments, including wheeled robots, quadcopters and quadrupeds . Federation costs consistency: constituents differ in action spaces, control rates, cameras and licenses. Moritz Reuss's review of VLA papers at ICLR 2026 calls OXE mostly low-quality data and notes that imitation learning still lacks good ways to quantify data quality . Re-Mix's learned domain weights beat uniform weighting by 38% on average on the data used to train the RT-X models . ## DROID: depth on one platform DROID's distinction is scene and site diversity: 76,000 trajectories totaling 350 hours, across 564 scenes and 86 tasks, gathered by 50 operators at 13 institutions over 12 months . Every trajectory came from one rig, a Franka Panda with two ZED 2 cameras and a ZED Mini wrist camera, [teleoperated](/data-hardware/teleop-rigs) through a Meta Quest 2. One platform gives one action space and one camera geometry, at the price of embodiment lock-in. Single-platform collections can be larger. RT-1's fleet of 13 robots gathered about 130k episodes over 17 months , and Language-Table released nearly 600,000 language-labelled trajectories . The Galaxea Open-World Dataset holds 500 hours across 50 scenes, all from one consistent robot embodiment . Diffusion policies trained on DROID beat policies trained on the next-best dataset by 22% in-distribution and 17% out-of-distribution . The project added language annotations for 75,000 episodes in December 2024 and improved camera calibrations for 36,000 in April 2025 . The paper releases DROID under CC BY 4.0 , whose deed allows commercial sharing and adaptation subject to attribution, a license link, change notices and the other license terms, and warns that other rights may limit a particular use . ## BridgeData V2: the academic workhorse BridgeData V2 holds 60,096 trajectories on a WidowX 250, a low-cost 6-DoF arm: 50,365 teleoperated demonstrations collected with a VR controller at 5 Hz and 9,731 scripted pick-and-place rollouts, across 24 environments and 13 skills . Trajectories average 38 timesteps . Its 2021 predecessor had 7,200 demonstrations of 71 tasks in 10 environments, and joint training with 50 demonstrations of a new task in a new domain doubled success on average . BridgeData V2's official project page states CC BY 4.0 for all data . The paper shipped baselines from goal-conditioned behavior cloning to ACT and RT-1 , and most of the data also ships inside OXE . ## AgiBot World: the corporate fleet AgiBot World's Beta release holds 1,001,552 trajectories totaling 2,976 hours, all from the AgiBot G1 platform with a multi-camera rig. AgiBot reports 217 tasks in five deployment scenarios and a 30% average gain over OXE pretraining for policies pretrained on its data, a vendor figure with no independent replication . IFR counts a record 5 million industrial robots operating worldwide in 2025, after more than 600,000 installations that year, 59 percent of them in China . ## The economics you can drag Drag the time to fix each jam and watch the payback change. Payback here divides cell capital by modeled monthly labour value, leaving out the damage and throughput savings in EVST's formula . This worked example has no measured deployment behind it, and each of its seven inputs is an assumption, labelled beside its control. The model also assumes 730 hours a month and a 60-month amortization period, counts modeled picks per elapsed hour, including downtime, and judges payback against a chosen 24-month horizon, the upper end of EVST's estimate for multi-shift palletising cells . At 15-second jam clearing, cutting per-pick success from 99.9 to 99 percent moves payback from 11.56 to 11.82 months, an increase of 2.2 percent. At 300 seconds the same cut moves payback from 12.11 to 17.30 months, and modeled output falls 30 percent, from 542.9 to 380.0 picks per elapsed hour. EVST, a vendor that quotes complete cells, publishes no fixed list prices and puts the robot at a third to half of total cell cost . ## What the installed base automates
IFR's World Robotics 2026, released on September 24, 2026, counts a record operational stock of 5 million industrial robots in 2025, up 9 percent, after more than 600,000 installations that year, up 11 percent. China installed 354,000 units, 59 percent of the total, and the United States, with almost 38,500 installations, passed Japan to become the second-largest market . A year earlier, World Robotics 2025 counted 4,663,698 robots in operation and 542,076 installed in 2024, above 500,000 in each year from 2021 . China then held 2,027,190, about 4.5 times second-ranked Japan's 450,530, and took 295,045 installations, 54 percent of the total . Strip the installed base down by task and most of it is repetitive motion in a fixed cell, with little or no perception worth the name. OSHA's Technical Manual lists uses including arc and resistance welding, painting and spraying, machine-tool loading and unloading, assembly, materials handling and packaging . In A3's North American order data for 2025, collaborative robots were 7,212 units worth \$241 million, 19.6 percent of the 36,766 robots ordered and 10.7 percent of the \$2.25 billion in order value. A3 began reporting them as a distinct category in Q1 2025 . Learned systems enter mostly through logistics. Automated storage and retrieval puts high-bay racking and shuttles where aisles and forklifts used to be, and AutoStore reports about 2,000 systems in 68 countries . Autonomous mobile robot fleets move cases and totes, and transport and logistics robots sold 117,500 units in 2025, 47 percent of the almost 250,000 professional service robots shipped that year, a total up 24 percent on 2024 . Goods-to-person stations bring the shelf to a stationary worker, which sets the productivity bar for automated piece picking. In October 2023 Amazon reported over 750,000 robots working collaboratively with employees; Sequoia was operating at one Houston fulfillment center, and testing Digit for tote recycling was planned . Its fleet overview, updated in June 2026, reports more than one million robots deployed since 2012, a cumulative total and not a simultaneous active-fleet count, with next-generation Proteus still a lab pilot . In September 2026 Amazon said its robots work across more than 300 facilities and assist employees with 75 percent of the customer orders it delivers . Its DeepFleet model was set to improve fleet travel efficiency by 10 percent . Amazon's Vulcan picks and stows approximately 75 percent of the types of items stored at its fulfillment centers, at speeds comparable to front-line employees. It hands items it cannot move to employees, and the post reports no pick-success rate or independently validated reliability . An Amazon Robotics paper on stowing into fabric pods does report outcomes: over 100,000 attempts in a fulfillment center, 85.86 percent succeeded, 9.31 percent were unproductive and 4.83 percent were defects . Symbotic's FY2025 Form 10-K reports about \$22.5 billion of backlog, meaning unperformed obligations under existing contracts and not revenue already earned, at September 27, 2025, against \$2.246922 billion of revenue for the year. Its Walmart agreement, expanded in May 2022, covers all 42 regional distribution centres, and Symbotic had 50 systems in deployment and 48 operational systems under software maintenance and support contracts . In November 2025 Kroger said it would close three automated fulfillment centres, in Wisconsin, Maryland and Florida, while monitoring the remaining facilities, and expected about \$2.6 billion of impairment and related charges . This is Money counted five remaining sites . On December 5, 2025 Ocado and Kroger agreed a one-off \$350 million payment that also covers Kroger's decision not to proceed with Charlotte. Ocado expects the closures to cut its FY26 fee revenue by about \$50 million . Ocado Intelligent Automation sells the same grid-robot warehouses outward into healthcare, third-party logistics and industrial parts . ## Humanoids in plants IFR counts about 7,000 [full-size humanoids](/data-hardware/hardware-taxonomy) sold in 2025 and says most applications remain specialized and often require human teleoperation . Agility says Digit 4 has logged more than 65,000 operational hours and moved 100,000 totes at GXO's Flowery Branch site at about 98 percent accuracy while on-task . Hyundai is training Atlas to sequence automotive parts at its Robotics Metaplant Application Center and expects component assembly by 2030 . Jonathan Hurst, Agility's cofounder and chief robot officer, wrote in IEEE Spectrum in October 2026 that in Digit 4's commercial deployments the robots had to work behind physical barriers, kept apart from people, to meet insurance and regulatory demands, which limited their usefulness . As a person approaches, Digit 5 is programmed to stop, set down its payload, sit on the floor and cut power to its motors before the person can touch it, which he calls "the only approach that makes sense as a first step" . Its safety sensors and computers, larger battery and stronger motors added bulk, and Digit 5 can no longer run or jump as earlier versions could . Figure's 11-month BMW deployment set an 84-second cycle requirement, a target above 99 percent success per shift and a goal of zero interventions. It reports 1,250+ hours of runtime and 90,000+ parts loaded, without achieved rates against those targets . Each of these figures comes from the company itself. Unitree's IPO prospectus adds the financial side: first-quarter 2026 revenue growth slowed to 68.49%, from 332.64% a year earlier, and adjusted net profit fell 52.55% year on year . ## The integrator's multiple A robot arm is a minority of what a cell costs. EVST puts complete palletising cells at two to three times the arm's price . Its July 15, 2026 commercial palletising-cell guide lists application-specific end-of-arm tooling, fencing, light curtains or area scanners, interlocked gates, safety-rated PLCs, installation, PLC/HMI integration, commissioning, pattern programming, software licences and any vision-guided pick logic for mixed loads. The surrounding-line work depends on what is already installed . OSHA's Technical Manual, discussing ANSI/RIA R15.06-2012, says the systems integrator completes and documents the application's risk assessment before commissioning and gives the results to the employer. Manufacturers or employers may also act as integrators. The employer retains responsibility for a safe workplace, and a risk assessment alone does not establish that the application protects workers . In its April 16, 2026 investor outlook, Bessemer predicts that near-term value will accrue to full-stack, vertically integrated players ahead of pure-play foundation-model companies. It says deployment requires domain-specific data collection, target-environment fine-tuning, hardware integration and operational infrastructure. It also stresses expensive data collection and foundation models not yet general enough to work out of the box . ## The metrics that decide a deployment Cycle time is the time required to produce a part or complete a process, measured for that operation . Takt time is available production time divided by customer demand, and its purpose is to match production with demand . NASA distinguishes inherent availability, computed from mean time between failures and mean time to repair without administrative, logistics or preventive-maintenance time, from operational availability, which includes them. Uptime is time in an operable state . The calculator above reports capital cost per modeled pick: robot price times the integration multiple, divided by modeled lifetime picks over a fixed amortization period. It does not include running costs. The payback period is total system capital cost divided by monthly labour, reduced-damage and throughput value. EVST's guide estimates 12 to 24 months for multi-shift palletising cells and 24 to 36 months for single-shift or lower-throughput operations . ## The jam rate is the lesson A separate authored example has no measured intervention rate behind it. At 99 percent per-pick success, with every failure needing a ten-second clearing, overhead is (1 − 0.99) × 10 = 0.1 seconds per attempted pick. Amazon's stow system is designed to stow 80 percent of warehouse items at 300 units per hour. A no-stow turnaway, when a pod leaves with nothing stowed, consumes at least 12 seconds . The intervention rate and clearing cost together decide whether a cell ships. Physical Intelligence reports that training on deployment data, including expert corrections during autonomous runs, more than doubled throughput and roughly halved the failure rate on some of its hardest tasks . Ken Goldberg proposes combining model-based engineering with model-free learning so robots can perform useful work, collect real-world data, and use those data to improve performance and learn adjacent skills. Goldberg does not claim that engineering removes the need for learning, and he expects model-free AI eventually to enable fully general-purpose robots . [The Reliability Gap](/frontier/reliability-gap) tracks the demo-to-production gap and selected deployment examples; [Autonomous Vehicles](/adjacent/autonomous-vehicles) covers the same question for driverless cars. Morgan Stanley's 2026 note on the humanoid industry's "PR problem", as reported by CNBC, describes [investors](/market-map) looking for real-world return on investment over polished demonstrations . Figure says its livestreamed logistics run lasted 200 hours , but it was one task at one site, with [no published success rate](/data-hardware/evaluation-crisis). ## Brownfield versus greenfield A greenfield site is designed around the automation: floor loading, ceiling height, power, network and traffic lanes exist because the system needed them. Amazon's Shreveport fulfillment center was built with 10 times more robotics, and its Sequoia can hold more than 30 million items . A brownfield deployment must fit the automation into a building that already runs. OSHA describes safeguards for non-collaborative robot applications during automatic operation: guards such as fences and barriers, interlocked guards and presence-sensing devices. Teaching inside the safeguarded space uses reduced-speed manual mode with an enabling device, and maintenance follows lockout/tagout procedures under 29 CFR 1910.147 or 29 CFR 1910.333 . Symbotic says it can install its systems in phases while the existing warehouse keeps operating . [Safety and Assurance](/frontier/safety-and-assurance) covers the wider obligations. ## The labour evidence, disagreement intact Daron Acemoglu and Pascual Restrepo find that one more robot per thousand workers cuts the US employment-to-population ratio by about 0.2 percentage points and wages by 0.42 percent. Losses concentrate in commuting zones exposed to industrial automation . In Germany, robot-driven displacement in manufacturing was fully offset by new jobs in services, and the cost fell mostly on young workers entering the labour force . Spanish manufacturers that adopted robots raised output by 20 to 25 percent within four years and created net jobs at a rate of 10 percent . French adopters also grew employment, at their competitors' expense, and the overall effect on industry employment was negative . The MIT Task Force on the Work of the Future, co-chaired by David Autor and David Mindell with Elisabeth Reynolds as executive director, found in 2020 no compelling evidence of a jobless future. It describes automation displacing some tasks and creating new work, shaped by economic incentives, policy choices and institutions .

Automated storage and retrieval puts high-bay racking and shuttles where aisles and forklifts used to be, and AutoStore reports about 2,000 systems in 68 countries . Goods-to-person stations bring the shelf to a stationary worker, which sets the productivity bar for automated piece picking. In October 2023 Amazon reported over 750,000 robots working collaboratively with employees; Sequoia was operating at one Houston fulfillment center, and testing Digit for tote recycling was planned . Its fleet overview, updated in June 2026, reports more than one million robots deployed since 2012, a cumulative total and not a simultaneous active-fleet count, with next-generation Proteus still a lab pilot . Its DeepFleet model was set to improve fleet travel efficiency by 10 percent . An Amazon Robotics paper on stowing into fabric pods does report outcomes: over 100,000 attempts in a fulfillment center, 85.86 percent succeeded, 9.31 percent were unproductive and 4.83 percent were defects . Its Walmart agreement, expanded in May 2022, covers all 42 regional distribution centres, and Symbotic had 50 systems in deployment and 48 operational systems under software maintenance and support contracts . In November 2025 Kroger said it would close three automated fulfillment centres, in Wisconsin, Maryland and Florida, while monitoring the remaining facilities, and expected about \$2.6 billion of impairment and related charges . This is Money counted five remaining sites . On December 5, 2025 Ocado and Kroger agreed a one-off \$350 million payment that also covers Kroger's decision not to proceed with Charlotte. Ocado Intelligent Automation sells the same grid-robot warehouses outward into healthcare, third-party logistics and industrial parts . ## Humanoids in plants IFR counts about 7,000 [full-size humanoids](/data-hardware/hardware-taxonomy) sold in 2025 and says most applications remain specialized and often require human teleoperation . Agility says Digit 4 has logged more than 65,000 operational hours and moved 100,000 totes at GXO's Flowery Branch site at about 98 percent accuracy while on-task . Hyundai is training Atlas to sequence automotive parts at its Robotics Metaplant Application Center and expects component assembly by 2030 . GXO and Agility's June 2024 agreement uses a robots-as-a-service model, with Digit moving totes from other robots to conveyors at a SPANX facility . Jonathan Hurst, Agility's cofounder and chief robot officer, wrote in IEEE Spectrum in October 2026 that in Digit 4's commercial deployments the robots had to work behind physical barriers, kept apart from people, to meet insurance and regulatory demands, which limited their usefulness . As a person approaches, Digit 5 is programmed to stop, set down its payload, sit on the floor and cut power to its motors before the person can touch it, which he calls "the only approach that makes sense as a first step" . Its safety sensors and computers, larger battery and stronger motors added bulk, and Digit 5 can no longer run or jump as earlier versions could . Figure's 11-month BMW deployment set an 84-second cycle requirement, a target above 99 percent success per shift and a goal of zero interventions. It reports 1,250+ hours of runtime and 90,000+ parts loaded, without achieved rates against those targets . Each of these figures comes from the company itself. Battery logistics also affect the operating cycle. Its July 15, 2026 commercial palletising-cell guide lists application-specific end-of-arm tooling, fencing, light curtains or area scanners, interlocked gates, safety-rated PLCs, installation, PLC/HMI integration, commissioning, pattern programming, software licences and any vision-guided pick logic for mixed loads. Morgan Stanley's 2026 note on the humanoid industry's "PR problem", as reported by CNBC, describes [investors](/market-map) looking for real-world return on investment over polished demonstrations . Amazon's Shreveport fulfillment center was built with 10 times more robotics, and its Sequoia can hold more than 30 million items . A brownfield deployment must fit the automation into a building that already runs. OSHA describes safeguards for non-collaborative robot applications during automatic operation: guards such as fences and barriers, interlocked guards and presence-sensing devices. Teaching inside the safeguarded space uses reduced-speed manual mode with an enabling device, and maintenance follows lockout/tagout procedures under 29 CFR 1910.147 or 29 CFR 1910.333 . Symbotic says it can install its systems in phases while the existing warehouse keeps operating . [Safety and Assurance](/frontier/safety-and-assurance) covers the wider obligations. ## The labour evidence, disagreement intact Daron Acemoglu and Pascual Restrepo find that one more robot per thousand workers cuts the US employment-to-population ratio by about 0.2 percentage points and wages by 0.42 percent. Losses concentrate in commuting zones exposed to industrial automation . It describes automation displacing some tasks and creating new work, shaped by economic incentives, policy choices and institutions .

## The comparison matrix VR system totals are unpublished; Meta lists the Quest 3S from \$299.99 . Try the Cost highlight. ## Bimanual workstations: fidelity first In ALOHA, an operator drives a leader arm that twins the follower, so demonstrations arrive in the robot's joint space. ACT, the [action-chunking](/manipulation/action-chunking) policy built for that rig, learned six bimanual tasks, each from about 10 minutes of demonstrations. It reached 84 to 96% final success on four of them, 64% on taping and 20% on threading a velcro tie. The paper put the bimanual setup at \$18k, or \$20k with add-ons such as cameras . Drag the copy's hand in the figure below and the robot arm mirrors it, recording each moment. Mobile ALOHA added a base; with 50 demonstrations per task and co-training on static ALOHA data, success rose by up to 90% on tasks like sauteing shrimp and opening a two-door wall cabinet . ALOHA 2's hardware designs are open source . The line now sells as Trossen AI at \$23,995.95 for the bimanual Stationary AI, \$33,695.95 for Mobile AI and \$4,545.95 for a single WidowX AI arm . RT-1's fleet of 13 robots gathered about 130k episodes over 17 months . ## GELLO: the kinematic twin GELLO is a scaled replica of the target arm built from 3D-printed links and off-the-shelf motors, so joint readings map one-to-one onto robot commands. Parts cost under \$300; the published designs cover Franka, UR5 and xArm. In its user study, 12 participants ran five tasks on a bimanual pair of UR5 arms, and GELLO was more reliable and faster than VR controllers or a 3D spacemouse. The \$300 buys a controller only, and every new arm needs its own design . A policy trained only on adapted AirExo-2 data performed comparably to one trained on teleoperated data . HOMIE's \$500 humanoid cockpit pairs an exoskeleton arm and motion-sensing gloves with a pedal-driven locomotion policy, finishing tasks in half the time of earlier systems . JoyLo+, from Wensi Ai, Jiajun Wu, Li Fei-Fei, Ruohan Zhang and colleagues at Stanford and Lambda (October 2026), puts motors on GELLO-style leader arms so they follow the policy, and a touch on a grip hands the whole robot to the operator for a correction . The two-arm leader set for a Galaxea R1 Pro costs about \$2,515 in parts . On four real household tasks with 25 trials each, 100 corrections over four retraining rounds raised average success by 81 percentage points, 30 more than 100 extra demonstrations . ## UMI: collection without a robot The UMI operator holds a 3D-printed parallel-jaw gripper with a wrist-mounted GoPro and a 155-degree fisheye lens; SLAM recovers the gripper pose from the video. The paper bills the printed gripper at \$73 and the GoPro and accessories at \$298, for a \$371 rig . On cup arrangement the project site reports 111 demonstrations per hour, against 35 for spacemouse teleoperation and 231 by bare hand . Latency matching at inference time and a camera-relative action representation let UMI policies deploy zero-shot on any arm with a compatible gripper and camera, shown on UR5 and Franka. The data lack a force channel . ForceMimic adds one: its operator peeled a zucchini in 5 minutes, against over 13 with force-feedback teleoperation . Four collectors gathered enough UMI data in one afternoon for about 90% success in new environments . A policy post-trained only on HiFi-UMI data matched in-domain teleoperation across three backbones . Pollen Robotics' Grabette (July 2026) is an open-source handheld recorder modelled on UMI that writes LeRobot datasets, with parts costing about €490. Its motorized twin, Gripette (about €120 in parts), is the robot-arm gripper that carries out the learned movements on a real or simulated arm . ## VR teleoperation: scale through headsets In VR teleoperation the robot mirrors the operator's hand or controller poses through a retargeting layer. In [DROID](/data-hardware/datasets), 50 operators at 13 institutions used Meta Quest 2 headsets on Franka Panda rigs to collect 76,000 trajectories totaling 350 hours over 12 months . Diffusion policies trained on that pool beat the next-best dataset by 22% in-distribution . RoboTurk's phone interface was statistically similar to VR controllers on task completion time . OPEN TEACH runs on a \$500 Meta Quest 3 at up to 90 Hz . Open-TeleVision renders the robot's surroundings in stereo and mirrors the operator's arm and hand motion on two humanoids . Bunny-VisionPro adds low-cost haptic feedback and collision and singularity avoidance in retargeting . The Apple Vision Pro it runs on launched at \$3,499 ; the October 2025 M5 model keeps that price . Human and robot arms share no kinematics; every action passes through IK and calibration. [HumanPlus](/rl-sim2real/humanoid-wbc) shadows a person from one RGB camera and reaches 60 to 100% success with up to 40 demonstrations . ## Gloves and wearables DexUMI's hand exoskeleton gives the operator direct haptic feedback and adapts human motion to feasible robot-hand motion, for an 86% average success rate . SEED-UMI collects data 3.0x faster than exoskeleton-based teleoperation . Sunday's Skill Capture Glove shares its robot hand's geometry and sensor layout; Sunday reports converting glove data to robot data with a 90% success rate . DITTO-X, from Stanford and Columbia researchers (September 2026), renders joint-level force and fingertip contacts from the robot hand and improved demonstration quality and throughput over a commercial hand-tracking glove . FOMO-Dex, from Ying Yuan, Jitendra Malik and colleagues at Amazon FAR and Carnegie Mellon (October 2026), hands force control to the robot: a controller between the operator's glove and a 22-DoF hand applies force-driven corrections along selected directions and leaves the rest of each command unchanged . Policies cloned from 50 such demonstrations averaged 6.3 screw turns per episode over 10 trials, against 0.6 from stiff-control data . Boston Dynamics argues that wearables capture only proxy signals for controlling a dexterous hand, and that reinforcement learning in simulation is an essential component . Apple's EgoDex recorded 829 hours with Vision Pro hand tracking ; Generalist AI reports over 270,000 hours for GEN-0 . ## Choosing by axis Leader arms and GELLO leave the smallest gap between collection and deployment; UMI, gloves and headsets scale across scenes, as DROID did . [The Data Bottleneck](/data-hardware/data-bottleneck) covers what the extra hours buy.

A success rate folds trial count, task length, scene setup and scorer into one number, and papers often report it with little or no information on the number of runs, initial conditions or success criteria .
## What the success rate hides: the horizon In an illustrative model, every decision succeeds with the same probability $p$ conditional on all earlier decisions succeeding, so a task of $n$ decisions completes with probability $p^n$ . At $p = 0.95$, 30 decisions give 21.5% and 100 give 0.6%. Drag "How many steps the job has" to compare these examples. Solving $p^n = q$ gives $p = q^{1/n}$, so an episode target of $q = 0.8$ needs 95.6% per step at $n = 5$ and 99.3% at $n = 30$. Behavior cloning compounds errors the same way: a policy with error rate $\varepsilon$ on the expert's states can make as many as $T^2\varepsilon$ mistakes over $T$ steps of its own . Benchmarks now measure long horizons directly. CALVIN scores 1,000 chains of five sequential tasks , and the 2026 BEHAVIOR Challenge ranks 100 full-length household tasks by average success with partial credit, with 20,000 teleoperated demonstrations totaling 1,950 hours . ## Small samples limit comparison Toyota Research Institute's Large Behavior Models extend the Diffusion Policy recipe to multitask models trained on about 1,700 demonstration hours. The mixture holds 468 hours of real bimanual teleoperation, 45 simulation hours, 32 UMI hours and about 1,150 hours from a subset of Open X-Embodiment . TRI reports 1,800 real-world rollouts and over 47,000 simulation rollouts, with 50 real attempts per task per policy per condition, a target of 200 in simulation and missing simulation data for some combinations. Hardware comparisons were blind, with policy order randomized within bundles sharing an initial condition . Simulation used automated predicates for scoring. TRI draws Bayesian posteriors over each policy's success probability under a uniform prior as violin plots, which avoid reading significance from overlapping confidence intervals; the posteriors describe single checkpoints and exclude variation from stochastic training. TRI also warns of a significant risk that many robotics papers measure statistical noise for lack of power . Snyder et al. give 10 or 50 trials as examples of small feasible samples, and a test that finds no significant difference does not show two policies are equivalent . Deep reinforcement learning met the same problem: without significance tests and standard reporting, claimed improvements are hard to judge , so interval estimates and performance profiles are advocated over point estimates . STEP, a sequential test from Snyder et al., stops comparing two policies once enough evidence accumulates. It reports up to 32% fewer trials than the Lai and SAVI sequential baselines, assumes i.i.d. binary outcomes and uses a uniform risk-accumulation schedule in its experiments . TRI uses the Lai test for binary comparisons, while STEP is a separate method, and Welch's t-test for task progress . A 2026 follow-up from Snyder and colleagues extends anytime-valid testing to partial credit and continuous metrics and reports up to 70% less evaluation effort than batch methods . ## Clean benchmarks overstate LIBERO reports 130 tasks: ten each in LIBERO-Spatial, LIBERO-Object and LIBERO-Goal, plus LIBERO-100: 90 short-horizon pretraining tasks and ten long-horizon downstream tasks. Each task has 50 human-expert demonstrations collected by Spacemouse teleoperation . LIBERO-Plus perturbs the benchmark along seven dimensions: object layout, camera viewpoint, robot initial state, language instruction, lighting, background texture and sensor noise. Models that score 95% on the clean benchmark fall below 30% under modest camera or initial-state shifts, and shuffling or removing the instruction barely moves performance, suggesting the models largely ignore the language . LIBERO-PRO reports that models above 90% on standard LIBERO collapse to 0.0% in its generalized setting , and THE COLOSSEUM measured 30 to 50% degradation per perturbation factor and at least 75% when perturbations combine . On RoboDojo's 42 simulated and 18 real tasks, the best of 30 policies in the standard setting scored 21.98 and fell to 1.57 under randomization, a 92.9% relative drop . On RoboCasa365's household tasks, the best multi-task baseline, GR00T N1.5, averaged 20.0% success . Newer benchmarks build the variation in. RoboTwin 2.0 randomizes clutter, lighting, background, tabletop height and language , and RoboLab's 120 tasks address the overlap between training and evaluation that trivializes success rates on existing benchmarks . ## Simulation as an evaluation proxy SIMPLER tests whether simulated performance predicts real performance . It narrows the visual gap with real-image backgrounds and matched textures, and the control gap by fitting controller stiffness and damping through offline system identification. The project site reports about 1,500 evaluation episodes each from real and simulated Google Robot and WidowX setups . Agreement is scored with Pearson correlation, which can be unstable when policies perform similarly, and Mean Maximum Rank Violation, which weights wrong orderings by real performance margins. It varies by task: the WidowX carrot-placement comparison contains a ranking error. The experiments focus on rigid objects, and green-screening assumes fixed cameras and misses shadows . Across 7 tasks and 5 policy architectures, SimFoundry's simulated evaluations reached a mean Pearson correlation of 0.911 with real results and a mean maximum rank violation of 0.018 . Generative world models now act as evaluators ([world-model evaluation](/world-models/evaluation)). Google DeepMind validated a Veo world simulator against 1,600+ real-world evaluations of eight Gemini Robotics checkpoints , WorldEval reports a strong correlation with real-world performance , and Ctrl-World, trained on DROID, ranks policies without real rollouts . SureSim corrects simulator bias with a few paired real and simulated trials and saves over 20 to 25% of hardware evaluation effort for similar bounds . [Sim-to-Real Transfer](/rl-sim2real/sim2real-transfer) covers simulation for training. WorldOracle, from Haoyi Duan, Yuke Zhu and colleagues at AgiBot, NVIDIA and three universities (October 2026), feeds recorded actions from real robot episodes to seven action-conditioned world models and scores whether each predicted video matches what happened . On 100 two-minute AgiBot G2 episodes, DreamDojo's single-view score out of 100 fell from 50.56 over the first 30 seconds to 27.08 over the full episode, and Cosmos 3 Nano's from 53.99 to 26.60 . AgiBot's own GE-Sim 2.0, which shares four authors with the benchmark, fell from 73.86 to 63.33 . ## Blind, distributed, pairwise RoboArena distributes evaluation across seven universities on the DROID Franka Panda platform . Evaluators receive anonymous policy endpoints, choose tasks and scenes, and run each pair double-blind and back-to-back from closely matched initial conditions, recording progress scores, preferences and explanations. Its study reports 612 pairwise comparisons across seven DROID-trained policies, and against a 4,284-rollout oracle its rankings agreed better than a conventional evaluation of 17 tasks and 44 episodes per policy . Chatbot Arena ranks language models the same pairwise, crowdsourced way, from over 240K votes . RoboChallenge hosts robots at its own site and exposes asynchronous observation and action APIs; model inference stays with the submitting user. Its first benchmark, Table30, holds tabletop tasks; held-out demonstration frames guide scene resets, but lighting and camera drift remain, and the system cannot verify the remote model matches its submitted name . OpenVLA's evaluation needed over 2,500 rollouts and over 100 hours of human labour, and AutoEval's automatic resets and success detection let evaluation run around the clock . XPolicyLab cuts the integrations needed to connect $N$ policies to $M$ environments from $O(NM)$ to $O(N+M)$ . ## Reading a result table - How many rollouts produced the number, and is its uncertainty reported ? - How long is the task? - What survives perturbation ? - Who scored the rollouts, with what agreement against the tested population ? - What correlation backs a simulation number ? StopWatch, from Xinhao Liu, Pieter Abbeel, Guanya Shi and colleagues at Amazon FAR, NYU, UC Berkeley and Carnegie Mellon (October 2026), checked the labels that score HM3D-OVON, an object-goal navigation benchmark. A stop counts only when the object's annotated name matches the goal word, so a robot that stops at a couch annotated as sofa fails when asked for a couch, and a manual audit dropped 23% of the unseen-category validation episodes for missing or wrong labels. The frontier-exploration expert that generated the training demonstrations succeeds in 72% of episodes under the official scoring and 96% under the authors' corrected scoring of the remaining episodes, and their system's lead over the strongest baseline, LightNav-0, grows from 6.4 to 8.8 points . Eval-Actions argues binary success rates hide process-level differences and provides 13K+ real-robot episodes over 150+ tasks , and fine-grained task progress separates policies with fewer trials than binary success . The [reliability gap](/frontier/reliability-gap) follows the same arithmetic into deployment.

Prices run from about \$122 in parts for an SO-101 arm to \$29,900 for a Unitree H2 humanoid , and Boston Dynamics has scheduled its 2026 Atlas deployments at Hyundai and Google DeepMind .
## The buyer's guide Try Preorder, Humanoids and \$1k-\$10k together and one row remains: Noetix's Bumi, announced for presale in October 2025 at ¥9,998, about \$1,400 . ## Arms, from \$122 to \$70,000 The SO-101 is a 3D-printed arm with six degrees of freedom, five joints plus a gripper, built from STS3215 servos. Its community BOM for one follower arm totals \$121.94 in the US column . Seeed Studio sells the SO-ARM101 Pro at \$295 unassembled or \$299 assembled, with 12-bit magnetic encoders and a 500 g payload . LeRobot runs ACT, π0 and SmolVLA policies on these arms . Pull the arm apart in the figure below, then guess which motor works hardest to hold it out straight. Trossen Robotics renamed its ALOHA line Trossen AI. Its Solo AI, Stationary AI and Mobile AI kits list at \$11,385.95, \$23,995.95 and \$33,695.95 and integrate LeRobot and OpenPI . The WidowX AI arm, sold in leader and follower forms for teleoperation, lists at \$4,545.95 in its base configuration, with six DoF, a 1.5 kg payload and 700 mm reach . ALOHA 2 succeeds the bimanual ALOHA rig behind ACT and Mobile ALOHA ; its hardware designs are open source, and the paper gives no price . Hugging Face, which bought Pollen Robotics in April 2025, sells the Reachy 2 humanoid for \$70,000 . The seven-DoF Franka Emika Panda collected DROID's 76,000 trajectories . ## Humanoids: shipping beat shouting Omdia counts about 13,000 [humanoids shipped](/market-map) in 2025, including 5,168 from AgiBot, 39 percent of the total , a figure that also counts its mobile manipulators . IFR counts about 7,000 full-size humanoids (above 140 cm) sold in 2025, often in applications still requiring human teleoperation . Unitree's May 2026 IPO prospectus reports over 5,500 humanoids shipped in 2025, excluding wheeled dual-arm robots, and calls that the world's highest total . Unitree's R1 AIR lists at \$4,900 with 20 DoF and the R1 at \$5,900 with 26 . The G1 lists at \$13,500 for the base model with 23 DoF, and its EDU configuration spans 23 to 43 DoF by quote . The H2 has [31 DoF](/how-robots-work/#humanoid) (six per leg, seven per arm, three waist, two head), 360 N·m of joint torque and a 2,070 TOPS onboard chip . 1X sells the NEO for \$20,000 or \$499 a month after a refundable \$200 deposit, with US deliveries starting in 2026 . In April 2026 it reported capacity for 10,000 NEOs a year and said some buyers would get theirs that year, others later . Boston Dynamics' electric Atlas has 56 DoF with continuous rotation at key joints, a 50 kg instant payload, IP67 sealing and a 4-hour swappable battery , and it reaches 2.3 m . Hyundai Motor Group plans 25,000 Atlas units for its plants over the next few years, plus a US factory able to build 30,000 robots a year . Figure's third-generation humanoid has a palm camera in each hand, no disclosed hand DoF and 2 kW wireless charging through its feet. Figure builds it for high-volume manufacturing at its BotQ facility , whose first line can make up to 12,000 humanoids a year . Agility says Digit 5, unveiled in September 2026, repeatedly lifts loads up to 22.7 kg and runs 90 minutes on a 9-minute charge, with general availability by the end of 2027 . Tesla says it is installing the first Optimus production lines at Fremont and will use the first builds to collect training data . ## Hands, bundled and standalone Most [dexterous hands](/frontier/dexterity) ship with a robot: Unitree's Dex3-1, a G1 EDU option, has seven active DoF per hand (three thumb, two index, two middle) and an optional tactile array . 1X's order page lists 22 DoF per NEO hand . Its July 9, 2026 hand post counts 25, adding 3 wrist DoF to the 22 fully actuated ones in the fingers and palm . Boston Dynamics' October 2026 Atlas hand has four fingers and 13 DoF, with pressure sensors over the fingertips and palm . The open LEAP Hand has 16 DoF and costs about \$2,000 in catalog parts, roughly an eighth of the Allegro Hand it was benchmarked against . RUKA's authors put the Allegro at \$15,000 and built a five-fingered hand for under \$1,300 . ORCA is an open 17-DoF tendon-driven hand with tactile sensors, under 2,000 CHF in materials , and the commercial Shadow Dexterous Hand uses 20 motors for 24 degrees of freedom . Sharpa's Wave, a human-scale five-finger hand with 22 active DoF and high-resolution tactile sensing, is sold through a sales enquiry and lists no price . PSYONIC designed its Ability Hand as a prosthesis and opened it to robotics researchers in November 2022 . ## Sensors: touch is the missing channel Generalist policies mostly train on vision and proprioception, and DROID's Franka rig has three cameras and no touch sensing . AgiBot World's humanoids add visuo-tactile sensors to the camera rig . A 2025 outlook in IEEE Transactions on Robotics blames divergent transduction methods with no standardized evaluation, poor durability, hysteresis and temperature sensitivity . Chris Paxton of Agility Robotics argued on October 12, after IROS 2026, that multi-fingered hands may need the touch sensing two-finger grippers can do without, because their fingers increasingly hide the contacts a camera would need to see. He called tendon-driven hands now sold off the shelf a significant step toward making human-like dexterity "an intelligence problem, instead of a hardware design problem" . The GelSight Mini retails at \$500 and Meta FAIR's open DIGIT fingertip at \$350 . DIGIT's successor, Digit 360, has about 8.3 million taxels and resolves normal and shear forces to 1.01 mN and 1.27 mN . GelSight manufactures it under a partnership Meta announced in October 2024 . AnySkin, a magnetic skin, is the first uncalibrated tactile sensor reported to carry learned policies across replacement skins . ## Compute: closing the loop NVIDIA's Jetson Thor T5000 delivers 2,070 sparse FP4 TFLOPS with 128 GB of LPDDR5X at 273 GB/s on a 14-core Neoverse-V3AE CPU, within 40-130 W. The T4000 has 1,200 TFLOPS and 64 GB . NVIDIA rates Thor at 7.5x the AI compute of Jetson Orin and launched the developer kit at \$3,499 in August 2025 . It now lists the kit at \$5,499, and the T5000 and T4000 modules at \$4,999 and \$2,999 in 1,000-unit volume . The 1X NEO runs on a Jetson Thor at up to 2,070 FP4 TFLOPS . Figure's Helix runs entirely on embedded low-power GPUs, with a 7-9 Hz vision-language model guiding a 200 Hz controller . VLA-Perf's roofline model predicts π0 inference at 19.0 Hz on Jetson Thor, 32.2 Hz on RTX 4090, 61.7 Hz on A100, 162.5 Hz on H100 and 314.4 Hz on B100, without network latency. These are batch-one analytical predictions for the 2.7B π0 baseline, with 3 cameras, 14 action dimensions, chunk size 50 and 10 denoising steps, and no measurements from running the policy on all five GPUs. On B100, raising denoising steps from 10 to 50 raises total latency 2.15×; raising chunk size from 50 to 250 raises it 11% . [Real-Time Execution](/manipulation/realtime-execution) develops these latency budgets. ## How to read these prices On July 28, 2026 the FCC added foreign-produced mobile robots, such as humanoids and quadrupeds, to its Covered List. A robot-learning system is a pipeline from physical events to decisions and back again; the checkpoint is one component among capture, schemas, training, evaluation, serving and recovery. The open-source LeRobot library spans that stack, from motor middleware to dataset storage, streaming and asynchronous inference <Cite id="lerobot-paper-2026" />.

<Image id="openvla-overview-2024" />

Machine learning systems often incur massive ongoing maintenance costs from data dependencies, configuration issues and hidden feedback loops <Cite id="hidden-technical-debt-2015" />. Splitting the stack into seven contracts, each with an artifact and a test, lets a failure be traced to one boundary. Try the check below; video alone only replays an episode.

<SelfCheck
  prompt="Which dataset record is sufficient to reconstruct one policy transition after the camera mount and training code change?"
  options={[
    {
      value: 'video-only',
      label: 'A compressed video and a final success label',
      why: 'This preserves appearance but loses robot state, action timing, transforms and the command that produced each transition.'
    },
    {
      value: 'tensor-only',
      label: 'The normalized, synchronized tensors consumed by one training run',
      why: 'Tensors help exact reruns but hide how units, frames and synchronization were derived. They cannot be reprocessed safely when the schema changes.'
    },
    {
      value: 'versioned-episode',
      label: 'Versioned raw streams with actions, transforms and calibration',
      why: 'This preserves the evidence needed to reconstruct features, audit alignment and migrate preprocessing while keeping provenance.'
    }
  ]}
  answer="versioned-episode"
  takeaway="Store raw, timed and versioned context to rebuild a transition; pixels alone let you watch it."
/>

## Contract 1: hardware and calibration

Record firmware, control mode and calibrated transforms for every camera, encoder, gripper and sensor: a dataset split cannot correct an unrecorded camera move. Time offsets between sensors are calibration parameters too, estimable together with the spatial ones <Cite id="kalibr-2013" />, and [calibration](/classical/calibration) covers the residuals.

<Image id="droid-camera-calibration-2024" />

## Contract 2: episode capture

An episode holds raw observations, robot state, commanded action, measured response, outcome, interventions and timestamps. ROS 2 Iron made MCAP its default bag format after testing found SQLite3 storage often not performant enough <Cite id="ros2-iron-mcap-2023" />. RLDS is a standard, lossless format for sharing episodes <Cite id="rlds-2021" />. Keep resets and failures: RoboMIND releases 5,000 real-world failure demonstrations with annotated causes <Cite id="robomind-2024" />.

DROID standardized [collection hardware](/data-hardware/teleop-rigs) and protocols across institutions to gather 76k in-the-wild trajectories <Cite id="droid-2024" />; <Term id="open-x-embodiment">Open X-Embodiment</Term> chose breadth, normalizing over one million trajectories across 22 embodiments <Cite id="open-x-embodiment-2023" />.

## Contract 3: a versioned training schema

Every preprocessing step, from frame selection to normalization and splits, needs a version. LeRobot provides datasets, policy implementations and tools around a common workflow <Cite id="lerobot-docs-2026" />. Its v3.0 format packs many episodes into each file after one file per episode hit file-system limits at millions of episodes <Cite id="lerobot-dataset-v3-2025" />.

Joint targets, Cartesian deltas and torques are different [action labels](/manipulation/action-spaces) even at equal array widths. Per-dimension binning tokenizers perform poorly on high-frequency dexterous data, and FAST+ is a universal tokenizer trained on 1M real trajectories <Cite id="pi0-fast-2025" />.

Split by the factor a claim generalizes across: random episode splits leak near-identical scenes. Across 15,000+ real rollouts, environment and object diversity mattered far more than demonstration count <Cite id="lin-data-scaling-laws-2024" />.

<SceneSplit className="my-6" />

## Contract 4: reproducible training

A training run saves configuration, code revision, dataset hash, seeds and normalization statistics with its weights. In robomimic's study of offline human demonstrations, recurrent behavior cloning was strong and the batch RL algorithms struggled to learn from the same data <Cite id="robomimic-2021" />.

OpenVLA is a public seven-billion-parameter VLA adapted on standardized robot trajectories <Cite id="openvla-2024" />, and the OpenVLA-OFT recipe raised its average LIBERO success from 76.5% to 97.1% and its action throughput 26-fold <Cite id="openvla-oft-2025" />. Physical Intelligence reports RECAP, which learns from deployment experience, more than doubles throughput on some of its hardest tasks <Cite id="pistar06-2025" />.

## Contract 5: simulation and offline evaluation

Isaac Lab supports large batches of robot-learning environments and sensor modalities <Cite id="isaac-lab-2025" />. Simulated scores help only when they rank policies as hardware does, which SIMPLER measures on matched tasks <Cite id="simpler-2024" />. PolaRiS rebuilds real scenes from short video scans and reports much stronger correlation with real performance than existing simulated benchmarks <Cite id="polaris-2025" />. SimFoundry reports a mean Pearson correlation of 0.911 across 7 tasks <Cite id="simfoundry-2026" />.

Co-training on simulated and real data raised real-world task performance by 38% on average <Cite id="sim-real-cotraining-2025" />.

## Contract 6: real-world evaluation

Papers often report success rates with little or no information on the number of runs, initial conditions or success criteria <Cite id="kress-gazit-evaluation-2024" />. LIBERO-Plus showed controlled perturbations across seven dimensions reveal robustness gaps that impressive benchmark success rates can mask <Cite id="libero-plus-2025" />; the [evaluation crisis](/data-hardware/evaluation-crisis) covers the statistics.

RoboArena ranks generalist policies through double-blind pairwise episodes run at several universities <Cite id="roboarena-2025" />. AutoEval runs evaluations around the clock <Cite id="autoeval-2025" />, and RoboDojo pairs 42 simulated and 18 real-world tasks <Cite id="robodojo-2026" />. A sequential test that can stop early cut evaluation burden by up to 70% against batch methods <Cite id="beyond-binary-success-2026" />.

## Contract 7: serving and robot integration

Production inference needs an observation assembler, model server, command gate, controller bridge and supervisor, with safety and high-rate feedback below the learned policy. ROS 2 was redesigned from the ground up because ROS 1 lacked production-grade features <Cite id="ros2-science-robotics-2022" />, and the [ROS 2 guide](/classical/ros2-for-ml-engineers) defines the interfaces. For the controller bridge, ros2_control is a ROS 2 framework for robot control, including real-time control. Its packages rewrite the ros_control packages of the original ROS to make new hardware simpler to integrate <Cite id="ros2-control-docs-2026" />. In September 2026 Intrinsic released Intrinsic Core, ROS-compatible real-time control, motion planning and Gazebo simulation under Apache 2.0 <Cite id="intrinsic-core-2026" />. The same month, Qualcomm agreed to acquire PickNik, the longtime steward of MoveIt <Cite id="qualcomm-picknik-2026" />.

Real-time chunking generates the next action chunk during execution, avoiding pauses at chunk boundaries <Cite id="real-time-chunking-2025" />, and SmolVLA decouples action prediction from execution <Cite id="smolvla-2025" />; [real-time execution](/manipulation/realtime-execution) has the latency budgets. Exploy, which the RAI Institute open-sourced on October 7, 2026, exports a PyTorch policy's observation code, network and action processing into one ONNX file for a C++ runtime. It checks numerical equivalence before hardware runs, and the institute says it already deploys policies on Spot, Atlas and the Unitree G1 <Cite id="exploy-2026" />.

## The data loop after deployment

In imitation learning, future observations depend on the policy's own actions, breaking the i.i.d. assumption of statistical learning <Cite id="dagger-2011" />. Failures should return to the dataset tagged with their cause. Sirius re-weights samples by approximated human trust and reports 27% higher real-hardware success than prior methods <Cite id="sirius-2022" />. CUPID shows under 33% of curated data can yield state-of-the-art diffusion policies on RoboMimic <Cite id="cupid-2025" />.

Mulligan, from Shuran Song, Chelsea Finn and colleagues at Stanford (October 2026), starts each round of supervised episodes at observed failures and untried object placements. With value-based action selection it raised final success on three real tasks by 10 to 34 percentage points, scored on 2,550 held-out, blinded episodes <Cite id="mulligan-2026" />.

## A minimal stack for a small team

Start with versioned episode files that are never edited in place, one versioned conversion command, a checkpoint registry, a deterministic offline test batch <Cite id="lerobot-dataset-v3-2025" /> <Cite id="hidden-technical-debt-2015" />, an evaluation sheet linked to episode IDs <Cite id="kress-gazit-evaluation-2024" />, and a policy process kept apart from command gating <Cite id="lerobot-paper-2026" /> <Cite id="safety-filter-2023" />.

Isaac Lab supports large batches of robot-learning environments and sensor modalities <Cite id="isaac-lab-2025" />. Simulated scores help only when they rank policies as hardware does, which SIMPLER measures on matched tasks <Cite id="simpler-2024" />. PolaRiS rebuilds real scenes from short video scans and reports much stronger correlation with real performance than existing simulated benchmarks <Cite id="polaris-2025" />. SimFoundry reports a mean Pearson correlation of 0.911 across 7 tasks <Cite id="simfoundry-2026" />.

Co-training on simulated and real data raised real-world task performance by 38% on average <Cite id="sim-real-cotraining-2025" />.

## Contract 6: real-world evaluation

Papers often report success rates with little or no information on the number of runs, initial conditions or success criteria <Cite id="kress-gazit-evaluation-2024" />. LIBERO-Plus showed controlled perturbations across seven dimensions reveal robustness gaps that impressive benchmark success rates can mask <Cite id="libero-plus-2025" />; the [evaluation crisis](/data-hardware/evaluation-crisis) covers the statistics.

RoboArena ranks generalist policies through double-blind pairwise episodes run at several universities <Cite id="roboarena-2025" />. AutoEval runs evaluations around the clock <Cite id="autoeval-2025" />, and RoboDojo pairs 42 simulated and 18 real-world tasks <Cite id="robodojo-2026" />. A sequential test that can stop early cut evaluation burden by up to 70% against batch methods <Cite id="beyond-binary-success-2026" />.

## Contract 7: serving and robot integration

Production inference needs an observation assembler, model server, command gate, controller bridge and supervisor, with safety and high-rate feedback below the learned policy. ROS 2 was redesigned from the ground up because ROS 1 lacked production-grade features <Cite id="ros2-science-robotics-2022" />, and the [ROS 2 guide](/classical/ros2-for-ml-engineers) defines the interfaces. For the controller bridge, ros2_control is a ROS 2 framework for robot control, including real-time control. Its packages rewrite the ros_control packages of the original ROS to make new hardware simpler to integrate <Cite id="ros2-control-docs-2026" />. In September 2026 Intrinsic released Intrinsic Core, ROS-compatible real-time control, motion planning and Gazebo simulation under Apache 2.0 <Cite id="intrinsic-core-2026" />. The same month, Qualcomm agreed to acquire PickNik, the longtime steward of MoveIt <Cite id="qualcomm-picknik-2026" />.

Real-time chunking generates the next action chunk during execution, avoiding pauses at chunk boundaries <Cite id="real-time-chunking-2025" />, and SmolVLA decouples action prediction from execution <Cite id="smolvla-2025" />; [real-time execution](/manipulation/realtime-execution) has the latency budgets. Exploy, which the RAI Institute open-sourced on October 7, 2026, exports a PyTorch policy's observation code, network and action processing into one ONNX file for a C++ runtime. It checks numerical equivalence before hardware runs, and the institute says it already deploys policies on Spot, Atlas and the Unitree G1 <Cite id="exploy-2026" />.

An ONNX file versions the graph representation and its operator sets <Cite id="onnx-ir-spec" />. ONNX Runtime partitions that graph across available execution providers <Cite id="onnx-runtime-architecture" />. A TensorRT engine is by default compatible only with the TensorRT version that built it; wider compatibility requires build-time configuration <Cite id="tensorrt-engine-compatibility-2026" />.

## The data loop after deployment

In imitation learning, future observations depend on the policy's own actions, breaking the i.i.d. assumption of statistical learning <Cite id="dagger-2011" />. Failures should return to the dataset tagged with their cause. Sirius re-weights samples by approximated human trust and reports 27% higher real-hardware success than prior methods <Cite id="sirius-2022" />. CUPID shows under 33% of curated data can yield state-of-the-art diffusion policies on RoboMimic <Cite id="cupid-2025" />.

Mulligan, from Shuran Song, Chelsea Finn and colleagues at Stanford (October 2026), starts each round of supervised episodes at observed failures and untried object placements. With value-based action selection it raised final success on three real tasks by 10 to 34 percentage points, scored on 2,550 held-out, blinded episodes <Cite id="mulligan-2026" />.

## A minimal stack for a small team

Start with versioned episode files that are never edited in place, one versioned conversion command, a checkpoint registry, a deterministic offline test batch <Cite id="lerobot-dataset-v3-2025" /> <Cite id="hidden-technical-debt-2015" />, an evaluation sheet linked to episode IDs <Cite id="kress-gazit-evaluation-2024" />, and a policy process kept apart from command gating <Cite id="lerobot-paper-2026" /> <Cite id="safety-filter-2023" />.

insertions.paragraph: Task repetition can sometimes be automated. Levine and colleagues collected grasp attempts without manual annotation or supervision; people replenished the object bins and started the system <Cite id="levine-hand-eye-2018" />.

Hand-object datasets make contact supervision explicit. ContactDB uses thermal imaging to record grasp-contact maps <Cite id="contactdb-2019" />; ContactPose pairs contact with hand pose, object pose and RGB-D images <Cite id="contactpose-2020" />. DexYCB benchmarks hand and object pose estimation and safe robot grasps for human-to-robot handover <Cite id="dexycb-2021" />.

HOI4D supplies egocentric RGB-D video with hand-pose, object-pose and action annotations <Cite id="hoi4d-2022" />. OakInk connects object affordances to recorded human interactions and transfers those interactions to virtual counterparts <Cite id="oakink-2022" />.

A benchmark score can also come from an analytic test. GraspNet-1Billion scores proposed grasp poses analytically and compares its evaluation system with physical experiments <Cite id="graspnet-1billion-2020" />.

Optical designs differ in the contacts they can observe. GelSlim 3.0 measures shape, contact-force distributions and incipient slip in a compact finger <Cite id="gelslim3-2021" />. GelTip views a deformable finger from its base, capturing contacts inside and outside the gripper closure <Cite id="geltip-2021" />. DenseTact estimates 3D surface deformation from fisheye camera images <Cite id="densetact-2022" />; AllSight estimates contact position, forces and torsion on a rounded finger <Cite id="allsight-2023" />.
Noetix lists Bumi at 98 cm tall and 17 kg, with 21 total degrees of freedom <Cite id="noetix-bumi-page-2026" />.

Configuration matters when comparing joint counts. Fourier lists up to 55 actuators for GR-3 with its optional 12-DoF hands <Cite id="fourier-gr3-docs-2026" />. LimX lists 31 active DoF for Oli and lists its end-effector options separately <Cite id="limx-oli-spec-2026" />.

Deformable-object benchmarks expose a different difficulty: the state has many interacting degrees of freedom and is only partly observed. SoftGym provides simulated manipulation tasks under a common interface for comparing algorithms on that problem <Cite id="softgym-2020" />.

Video corpora supply different supervision. EPIC-KITCHENS labels unscripted kitchen activities using participants' retrospective narrations <Cite id="epic-kitchens-2018" />. HowTo100M uses automatically transcribed instructional videos <Cite id="howto100m-2019" />, while COIN adds step descriptions and their time boundaries <Cite id="coin-video-2019" />.

Other datasets change the views or action vocabulary. Ego-Exo4D synchronizes first- and third-person recordings of skilled activities <Cite id="ego-exo4d-2023" />. Something-Something defines video classes through caption templates aimed at physical common-sense understanding <Cite id="something-video-2017" />.

Generative models can also augment existing observations. GenAug uses pretrained image-text models to make semantic variations of tabletop manipulation training data and tests transfer to new scenes and objects <Cite id="genaug-2023" />.

A physical benchmark also needs repeatable setup. FurnitureBench supplies printable furniture parts, demonstrations and systematic task initialization for real-world assembly, alongside a corresponding simulator <Cite id="furniturebench-2023" />.

insertions.paragraph: Visual teleoperation can start from different observations. DexPilot controls a hand-arm system by observing the operator's bare hand <Cite id="dexpilot-2019" />; TeachNet maps human-hand depth images directly to robot joint angles <Cite id="teachnet-2018" />. AnyTeleop supports different arms, hands and camera configurations within one system <Cite id="anyteleop-2023" />. Holo-Dex uses a headset's hand-pose estimator to collect demonstrations, then combines learned features with non-parametric imitation <Cite id="holo-dex-2022" />.

DexCap records wrist and finger motion with SLAM and electromagnetic tracking, alongside 3D observations of the scene. Its DexIL algorithm combines inverse kinematics with point-cloud imitation learning to transfer those motions to a robot hand <Cite id="dexcap-2024" />.

Object models supply another kind of supervision. ShapeNet organizes CAD models by semantic category and records attributes such as alignment and size <Cite id="shapenet-2015" />. PartNet adds detailed hierarchical part labels <Cite id="partnet-2018" />; ABC retains explicitly parameterized curves and surfaces for geometric ground truth <Cite id="abc-models-2018" />. The YCB set pairs physical everyday objects with scans, physical properties, geometric models and example manipulation protocols <Cite id="ycb-models-2015" />.

For control comparisons, safe-control-gym exposes symbolic dynamics and constraints and lets experiments repeat disturbances to controls, measurements and inertial properties. That makes the disturbance protocol part of the benchmark <Cite id="safe-control-gym-2021" />.
